entries.title: P0117 referee scope: independent thin-tube obstruction
entries.statement: Independent referee check on 2026-10-10: for iid finite nonnegative nonconstant nearest-neighbor edge weights on Z^2, w390's explicit high-slab and cheap-bypass construction proves that no injective ambient geodesic ray can eventually stay in a deterministic axis-aligned tube |y-y0|<=w(|x|) when w is nondecreasing and limsup w(n)/sqrt(log n)<1/sqrt(C), with C determined by two positive-probability weight thresholds as in the source proof. This is a partial theorem about confined rays. It does not exclude an unrestricted bigeodesic, since no valid step confines every bigeodesic to such a tube.
assumptions: iid finite nonnegative nonconstant edge weights on undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2
fixed deterministic nondecreasing tube width and integer center

entries.title: P0117 source status: 2026 primary preprint claim
entries.statement: The 2015 Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey asks in Question 31 whether geodesic lines exist. A September 24, 2026 primary preprint titled No bigeodesics in planar first-passage percolation explicitly claims simultaneous absence of all bigeodesics for iid nonnegative nonatomic Z^2 edge weights when the minimum of four independent weights has finite second moment. The theorem statement was checked on 2026-10-10, but its full proof was not audited in this referee packet. Therefore the 2026-09-07 attempted-unsolved ledger tag is stale as an openness claim; current proof acceptance remains unverified here.
assumptions: the preprint theorem statement has been read, not independently proved

relations.rationale: The reviewed thin-tube theorem is a partial, explicitly scoped result on the same FPP bigeodesic target; it does not prove that target.
The historical preprint-status record corrects the dated target's implied current-open label without asserting proof acceptance.
